verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Coimbatore pump and valve makers with export or organised-OEM order books and copper pass-through clauses; avoid pure domestic agri-pump assemblers and government-tender-dependent units until TN GST trend and copper costs stabilise.
title: Coimbatore Pumps, Motors & Valves: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Coimbatore has been a pump cluster since 1926, built on component suppliers, engineering specialists and testing facilities, and it is now shifting from agricultural and domestic water pumps to high-end, smart and specialised industrial pumping systems for global markets [3].** Cash comes from converting castings, copper windings, stampings and bought-out motors into pump sets sold either to OEMs, dealers or government tenders. Value sits in the impeller and motor design and in the test certification, not in the assembly shed. The cluster has an import-substitution push, with SITARC (SIEMA and CODISSIA) developing an indigenous submersible slurry pump previously sourced overseas [3].

## Where cash and risk sit now
**Copper is the swing factor: Coimbatore MSMEs have seen copper roughly double within a year to 1500 rupee/kg, with input cost moving from 500 rupee, and orders are being hit [2].** Rating agencies flag exactly this: C.R.I. Pumps' margins are susceptible to volatile raw material prices, operations are working-capital intensive, and pass-through ability is only moderate in a competitive market [10]. So when a proposal lands, check the copper pass-through clause in the order; if pricing is fixed-price on a six-month contract, ask for the raw-material escalation clause or cut the tenor. **The local demand signal is weak: Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 9.3 pp slower [D].** That is a state-level stress signal, not a Coimbatore-specific one; the sources say little about this city's own order flow, so lean on first principles and peers.

## The growth opportunity
**India-wide, NIC 28 output is +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date, and exports are +19.8% Apr-to-date in USD [D] — the demand is in export and organised-OEM channels, not local agri retail.** Peer results confirm the split: Shakti Pumps grew revenue 37.9% YoY to Rs 858.67 crore in Q1 FY27 but PAT fell 46.72% YoY to Rs 51.59 crore [5], while Oswal Pumps grew FY26 operating income 44.3% YoY to INR 2,064 crore with Q4 margins moderating to 23.2% on competitive tender pricing and input costs [7]. Pursue exporters and tier-2 suppliers to these OEMs, and units with slurry, sewage and industrial pump order books [3]. Avoid pure government-tender players: Shakti's Karnataka order is about 35% of its order book and the state's dues reached a high in January 2026 [6].

## How to grow safely
**Structure for the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet: cash-flow lending against verified order books, with monthly stock and debtor statements as a condition.** Take copper price and inventory quantity every month, plus the order-book position split domestic versus export. Covenant on debtor days and on the share of government receivables; if government dues cross a third of the book, ask for escrow of tender proceeds. Cap capex-funded term loans to units that have already demonstrated export invoicing, since rating reports show capex and working capital both pulling on debt [9].

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for margin compression before it shows in GST: ICRA's negative trigger for KSB is operating margin below 9.5% on a sustained basis or rising working-capital intensity [8].** If a unit's margin slips toward that line while copper stays at 1500 rupee/kg [2], reduce exposure. If monthly GST on outward supplies falls for two quarters while TN state GST stays negative [D], treat it as order loss, not timing.
watch: price stays at 1500 rupee/kg [2] with no pass-through clause -> reprice limit or demand escalation clause
two quarters of decline while TN GST stays at -3.2% [D] -> shift to cash-flow lending only
Debtor days and government receivable share (monthly)
government dues cross one-third of book, as with Shakti's Karnataka exposure [6] -> escrow tender proceeds
margin falls below 9.5% sustained [8] -> reduce limit and review tenor
export share falls and domestic tender share rises -> cap fresh exposure
